SECTION_C1_PIN_CORRECTION.the_defect_explained: v1.0.1 was authored across two commits: an initial commit, then a second correction (adding finding OF-C7) via git commit --amend, which REWRITES the commit and therefore changes every blob's parent tree even where the blob's own content is unchanged. Between those two commits, this lane captured the two v1.0.0 blob SHAs with `git ls-tree -r HEAD` -- true of the FIRST commit -- and then used that captured value as a pin inside v1.0.1's own text, which was written and committed only in the SECOND, amended commit. The pin therefore named a blob that was correct at the moment it was measured but stale by the moment it was written down, and it was never re-derived at the point of writing.
SECTION_C1_PIN_CORRECTION.why_it_matters: A pin that says 'MANDATORY AND VERIFIED' and is wrong teaches a certifier the wrong lesson twice: once by being wrong, and once by demonstrating that this chain's own verification language is not a reliable signal of verification having actually happened. The fix is not merely swapping in the right value; it is stating the METHOD precisely enough that the same failure mode is structurally harder to repeat.

the_correct_derivation.rule: A blob pin for 'the file as committed' is derived from the COMMITTED OBJECT, never from a working-tree hash taken at an earlier point in the lane and carried forward by memory or by copy-paste.
the_correct_derivation.method: git rev-parse <commit-or-HEAD>:<repo-relative-path>. Cross-checked against git hash-object <path> on a clean, unmodified working tree at the same commit, and against git rev-parse <the specific commit that introduced the file>:<path>. All three must agree; if they do not, the working tree has diverged from what is committed and the pin is not yet derivable.
the_correct_derivation.when_to_re_derive: At the MOMENT the pin is written into a new file, never earlier. A value captured during exploration, before the file containing the pin is itself finalized and committed, is a DRAFT value and must not be copied into committed prose without being re-checked at the point of commit.

SECTION_C5_EXPOSURE_VS_OCCUPANCY.the_gap: v1.0.1's corrected G-N3 ground text reads, in part: 'a reachable, healthy GoTrue is a client surface for token refresh... and nothing... disables the refresh-token grant for a session issued before, or through a channel outside, those flags.' This is written in a way that can be read as asserting that a write IS occurring -- that a session exists and IS refreshing -- when what this census actually measures is only that the SURFACE is open. Whether any session in fact exists to use it is exactly the OCCUPANCY question Tier 2 (pg_stat_activity) would answer, and Tier 2 is not conferred. G-N3 must stay fail-closed on the exposure fact alone; it must not be read as claiming the occupancy fact was measured.

the_distinction_stated_and_bound_to_G_N3.EXPOSURE: Whether the write SURFACE is reachable and enabled -- what OBS-S2/OBS-S3 actually measure. A healthy, internet-reachable Auth service is EXPOSURE. This is a TIER 1 fact and this census measures it directly.
the_distinction_stated_and_bound_to_G_N3.OCCUPANCY: Whether a WRITER -- a session, a scheduled job, an in-flight request -- actually exists right now to use that surface. This is a TIER 2 fact (pg_stat_activity, cron.job, the pg_net queue) and this census does NOT measure it, per DEP-C1.
the_distinction_stated_and_bound_to_G_N3.why_G_N3_correctly_fires_on_exposure_alo: The parent's own W-4 measurement establishes that NO ACT available to this chain can distinguish an exposed-but-unoccupied surface from an exposed-and-occupied one without a Tier 2 read, and that the cost of guessing wrong is a write inside the window whose emptiness is the whole question. Firing on exposure alone is therefore the FAIL-CLOSED choice given what is actually measurable at Tier 1 -- not a claim that occupancy was observed.
the_distinction_stated_and_bound_to_G_N3.the_corrected_ground_text: 'A reachable, healthy GoTrue is a client surface a session COULD use for token refresh, independent of sign-up/sign-in configuration -- disable_signup and the external-provider flags govern whether a NEW client can authenticate, not whether an ALREADY-ISSUED token can be refreshed. This census does NOT measure whether such a session in fact exists (that is OCCUPANCY, a Tier 2 fact under DEP-C1); it measures only that the surface is EXPOSED. G-N3 fires on exposure alone because this chain has no Tier 1 way to rule occupancy out, and treating an unmeasured occupancy question as favourable would be reading a Tier 2 UNKNOWN as a negative, which SECTION_F already forbids by name.'
the_distinction_stated_and_bound_to_G_N3.no_rule_changes: G-N3's CONDITION (Auth reachable and healthy) is unchanged by this correction. Only the GROUND -- the prose justifying why that condition is the right one -- is corrected, to stop it reading as an occupancy claim this census never made.

SECTION_C5_EXPOSURE_VS_OCCUPANCY.consequence_for_the_evidence_package: Where G-N3 fires, the evidence package's per-observation `verdict` field (SECTION_H) records the classification as 'EXPOSED -- OCCUPANCY UNMEASURED', never as 'WRITER PRESENT' or any phrasing implying a session was actually observed. This is a wording requirement on the future execution lane's evidence output, stated here so it does not have to be improvised at that lane's own writing time.
